prose_updates.tldr: In a designed-depletion or calibrated loss-to-follow-up regime, the censoring time is the earlier of two conditionally independent continuous loss or availability times whose near-horizon survivals vanish linearly, giving the known quadratic endpoint order while leaving the smooth residual censoring law unknown. At the scientific horizon, this quadratic censoring makes the influence function for survival itself non-square-integrable, but the remaining-life factor in fixed-endpoint RMST cancels one endpoint power and leaves a finite efficiency bound. The paper constructs a total cross-fitted one-step estimator that attains that bound uniformly over the stated radius-20 Hölder primitive class while learning the treatment propensity, event hazard, and rescaled censoring residual. Simultaneous local-cubic concentration in the last time--covariate cells gives nuisance rate \((\log n/n)^{1/3}\), and a terminal-strip Fano packing proves a matching minimax sup-norm lower bound for learning the event hazard over the same primitive class. This sharp primitive rate, exact product drift, weak \(5/2\)-moment Studentization, canonical-gradient certificate, and uniform Wald coverage form the publishable kernel.

project_justification.fill: The project integrates the survival score before analysis, learns the smooth event hazard and \(q_a=S_ag_a\) by boundary-adaptive cubic risk-set equations, proves their terminal-cell \((\log n/n)^{1/3}\) rate without assuming it, and matches the event-hazard upper rate by a same-class terminal-strip Fano lower bound. It then propagates the exact product drift through cross-fitting and proves variance consistency and a uniform Studentized limit from a \(5/2\)-moment envelope.

prose_updates.honest_scope: Identification of the fixed contrast is standard. Estimation and inference at the quadratic endpoint are resolved here for the stated primitive class. The theorem fixes the horizon \(1\), censoring exponent \(2\), one-dimensional covariate, smoothness order \(4\), and all radius and band constants. Within this class, the learned event-hazard sup-norm rate \((\log n/n)^{1/3}\) is minimax sharp; the converse does not claim a minimax lower bound for RMST risk or for each other nuisance separately. The result does not cover an estimated endpoint exponent, a shorter moving horizon, a parametric hazard subclass, or a different target. As an in-class sanity check, fix \(\delta\in(0,1)\), set \(\tau:=1-\delta\), and diagnostically restrict the same factor-preserving learner and score integrals to \([0,\tau]\). Every \(P\in\mathcal P_4\) then obeys \(G_a(t\mid x)\ge\delta^2/2\) on \([0,\tau]\), so the construction is compared in the ordinary positive-follow-up regime covered by Westling et al. (2024), while retaining its factor-preserving algebra. This diagnostic restriction is only a sanity check and does not change the fixed horizon-\(1\) target or introduce a censoring-floor assumption into the main result. The general censoring-exponent phase diagram remains a separate flagship question.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem derives simultaneous finite-sample control of the random at-risk Gram matrices, martingale and direct-risk numerators, cubic Taylor remainders, clipping, division, and deterministic fallbacks under only the primitive class bands. The resulting \((\log M/M)^{1/3}\) upper rate is paired with \(\textnormal{thm:primitive-endpoint-minimax-lower-bound}\), whose legal terminal-strip Fano subclass has information \(O(Mh^{12})\) and separation \(h^4\).
statement_notes.gap: Closed: the last-cell concentration bound holds uniformly under arbitrary measurable band-bounded covariate density, and the event-hazard sup-norm exponent is minimax sharp over the same \(\mathcal P_4\).
